newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols weaken after auction.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols weaken after auction.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options weakened in late trade as underlying bond prices recouped early losses on better than expected results of the Treasury's 30-year bond auction, dealers said.
Front months were the hardest hit as event-risk premium evaporated and time-decay weighed heavily.
"We rallied back unchanged (in futures) and they're crushing the December (volatilities)," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Implied volatility for December T-bond futures options tumbled nearly a full percentage point from Wednesday's closing level to about 8.0 percent. December contracts expire Friday next week.
December futures jumped half a point soon after the auction results, climbing above Wednesday's close. The contract had sunk to a low of 112-29/32 earlier.
An investment bank was seen selling part of the 5,000 contracts of December 115 calls it had bought a few days ago. It also bought 5,000 lots of 114 calls earlier in the day when futures were lower.
Implied volatility for March T-bond options was a touch softer at about 9.7 percent.
The Treasury's $10 billion auction of 30-year bonds produced an average yield of 6.619 percent, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.68 times.
All in all, the market appeared to have digested the new Treasury offerings this week fairly well, traders said.

Many gamma players who bought large lots of out-of-the money options -- even calls -- prior to the auctions and Tuesday's U.S. elections, when December volatility was around 10 percent, were seen to have been money losers.
The shorter end of the yield curve was relatively quiet.

Implied volatilities for Eurodollar futures options were steady as futures erased minor early losses. Traders said concerns stemming from the dollar's decline overnight and uncertainties over President Bill Clinton's economic policies in his new administration were supporting volatilities.
Implied volatility for March Eurodollar futures options gained about 0.1 point to 11.9 percent.
"It's been kind of a light bid to the market without a lot of participation," said an investment bank trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Still, he said, the March 94.25 and 94.50 calls saw relatively good buying. March futures were up one basis point to 94.47 in late trade.

With the U.S. Veterans Day partial holiday coming up, traders expected little activity until next week's inflation numbers. The October producer price index is due out on Wednesday and the consumer price index on Thursday.
CME interest rate products will trade a full day on Friday but close early on Monday, while CBOT T-bond derivatives will close early on Friday and trade normal hours on Monday.
